The trader uses a model that predicts the probability of an uptick and a downtick in the value of a basket of stocks based on past data to predict the daily uptick and downtick percentage in the market from the end of the day. #### Part 2: Probability of an Upturn Percentage

The probability of an uptick in the value of a basket of stocks is 0.9, while the probability of a downtick is 0.7.

To create a correctly scaled probability distribution for an uptick and a downtick, we create a discrete random variable \(X\) that takes values from the intervals \((0,1)\), \((1,2)\), \((2,3)\), \((3,4)\), \((4,5)\), and so on up to \((0.9,1)\). The cumulative distribution function \(F(x)\) of \(X\) is then:

\[
F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} P(X \leq n) = P(X \leq x) + P(X \leq x+1) \\
